content:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT detected: latency SLO breach on /v1/generate (p99 > 2.5s). Paging oncall.

jamie: I'm on it. paging @kyle (primary) and @devon (infra). @marie can you join for runtime/GPU checks? :wave:

kyle: checking grafana now. can someone drop the link to the dashboard?

jamie: https://grafana.internal/redwood/latency?panel=service-v1-generate — p95 ~ 600ms -> 1.2s, p99 trending up to 3.4s, tails spiking in the last 7m.

marie: seeing streaming stalls in the traces: lots of idle time waiting on GPU kernels, spikes align with nodes 10-12 in gpu-pool-2.

devon: I see node 10 reporting repeated ECC corrected errors in syslog. grabbing kernel logs.

devon: log snippet:
```
Mar 12 14:03:21 gpu-node-10 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, PID: 1234, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 12 14:03:25 gpu-node-10 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 43, ECC error detected, corrected
Mar 12 14:04:00 gpu-node-10 thermal: GPU temp=92C throttle=1
```

marie: `nvidia-smi` snapshot from node-10:
```
GPU  Temp  Pwr  Ecc-Errs
0    92C   250W  corrected=12
```

kyle: thermal 92C and ECC corrections — likely thermal throttling + flaky memory. That would explain tail stalls: kernel retries and long scheduling pauses.

jamie: impact assessment: streaming endpoints show ~3% increased user-facing stalls (clients seeing stalled stream chunks and reconnects). One enterprise customer (acct: acme-corp) reported degraded interactive response times. CS notified.

customer-success: confirmed, acme reported 60 sessions affected, some timed out at client side after 8s. We have a support ticket open (SUP-3245) and informed them we're triaging.

devon: mitigation plan proposal:
- cordon gpu-node-10 from pool-2
- drain running containers on node-10 (live migrate/or restart on other nodes)
- scale up pool-2 by +2 spare nodes while we drain
- failover traffic for latency-sensitive routes to dedicated low-latency pool (pool-1) for 30m

kyle: agreed. I'll run cordon+drain and scale commands. Also suggest enabling model-fallback to quantized variant for new requests to reduce GPU power/heat for the short window.

marie: enabling fallback: route policy update applied: for /v1/generate model=big-llama -> fallback=big-llama-8q when p99>2s. Patch applied to router config.

kyle: running commands now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-10 --context=prod
kubectl drain gpu-node-10 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --context=prod
scale pool-2 --replicas +2
```

kyle: drain in progress, 6 pods rescheduled. starting scale up.

oncall-bot: NOTE: automatic alert suppressed for node 10 during drain window (15m).

marie: traffic routing change confirmed. new requests are hitting quantized variant. p95 drops from 1.2s -> 700ms after fallback; p99 slowly trending down.

jamie: keep an eye on tail latency and streaming stalls. devon, once drain completes, can you attempt a soft reboot and run hardware diagnostics (memtest/GPU diag) on node-10?

devon: yes. planning to run vendor diagnostics. suspect ECC counts will continue to increase under sustained load — likely RMA.

kyle: scale up finished, routing shifted. p99 now 1.1s and falling. streaming stalls metric (streaming.stalls/sec) reduced from 0.22 -> 0.06.

marie: traced a stalled RT stream: server was waiting 12s between token send calls while GPU was throttled. root cause consistent with thermal/PCI resets.

devon: after drain, soft rebooted node-10 and ran pci rescan. gpu driver showed immediate ECC increment on stress test. attaching diag output:
```
GPU0 ECC corrected: 23 -> 45 under 120s stress
Thermal threshold hit: 95C
Result: intermittent PCI resets and Xid 43/79
```

kyle: taking node-10 OOS. marking as degraded in inventory and creating HW ticket for vendor RMA (HW-9872).

jamie: mitigation checklist complete? any active customer impact still unfolding?

customer-success: acme still seeing some sessions delayed for older sessions pinned to node-10; advise forced reconnects from our side for those sessions. CS pushing patch to reconnect flow.

marie: we can expedite by invalidating KV cache for sessions pinned to node-10 and forcing session resync. I'll run that for affected sessions list from logs (SUP-3245 subset).

devon: creating incident record in Jira: RED-INC-20260312, adding logs and diag output. tagging hardware RMA.

sre-lead: taking handoff at 18:00 UTC. jamie, please summarize current state and next actions for the oncall change.

jamie: summary for handoff:
- Root cause: GPU node-10 showing ECC corrected error growth + thermal throttling -> PCI resets -> increased p99/tail latency + streaming stalls.
- Mitigation: cordoned+drained node-10, scaled pool-2 +2, route fallback to quantized model, forced reconns for affected sessions.
- Customer impact: acme-corp ~60 sessions affected; overall platform tail latency spike, 3% increase in streaming stalls, now mitigated to background.
- Next actions: vendor RMA for node-10 (HW-9872), run extended stress on replacement, improve thermal monitoring (alert at 85C instead of 90C), add ECC counter alert on nodes.

sre-lead: ok taking over. will own postmortem and follow-ups. assign to @devon for RMA coordination and @marie for runtime fallback tuning. reopen if p99 > 1.5s.

jamie: thanks team. moving to post-incident review doc. tagging this thread for postmortem.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT resolved (mitigation applied). creating incident timeline and summary. severity: Sev3 -> monitoring phase.

customer-success: acme confirmed recovery; closing support ticket after final verification.

marie: note for follow-up: add automated fallback to quantized variant for streaming sessions >512 tokens to proactively reduce thermal load on older hardware.

devon: ordering replacement GPU nodes; tracking RMA. will update RED-INC-20260312 with ETA.

sre-lead: handoff complete. keep the ticket open until RMA closed and alert thresholds adjusted. good triage and coordination. :thumbsup:"
